The reason I have kept this new stuff separate for the time being is because I don't want to have to worry about breaking the existing site as I develop the new stuff. OK - seems like verification is not working at all and where we stand with DecideAI is pretty unclear. I think the immediate course of action for us should be to suspend the feature. This will essentially hide the feature from the front end and make the isVerified state just resolve to true everywhere it is used in the system for the time being. This will just level the playing field until we can figure out what to do. 

Next step would be to replace the concept with something that works. Now in an ideal world this would be an IC native service but as of right now I do not see that that is viable. The process of verification of unique personhood is comprised of a few steps. The storing of some vector representing the user's data and the comparison of subsequent submissions to confirm continuous identity over time can certain be done in a canister. But the actual conversion of someone's video feed into that vector and a judgement about whether or not they are a live real person is something that requires a model that cannot viably be run in a canister AFAIK. So this means we probably _always_ need to rely on _some_ third party or at least some off-chain component to do that. 

At least, that is if we take that kind of approach to the problem. It is arguably not the only approach. We could also take the view that we should redefine what verification _means_ and come up with something that is instead based on behavioural heuristics (account longevity, interaction patterns, peer endorsements etc). This is also an interesting idea although pretty fraught with difficulty around making it fair and resistant to gaming.

suspending the verification for now is the right architectural move to keep things level, oin the tech constraint we would not run heavy extraction inside the ic cannister, feature extraction can run clientside in the browser, where the browser generates the mathematical vector or commitment, and only a lightweight prof score is sent to the camister for comparison, webauthn passkeys can also help with user presence and device level verification, though i would not treat that as perfect liveness by itself, rrthat said, shifting to behavoipral heuristics is a much stronger web3 architecture, dropping biometrics and relying on on chain history, account age, account behavior, and peer endorsements removes the biggest privacy and third party data concerns, we should focus on building out that native reputation layer instead of dealing with biometric api.

I think there is certainly some uncertainty around whether it is possible / feasible to do that extraction of vectors from video data on the client in the browser. I would love to be pointed at some library or technique that can do that. In parallel it would be good to steelman a reputation mechanism that crucially cannot be gamed.
